advances: A fiberwise cap calculus for polytopes, including positive-area supporting facets.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
For $d=1$, use the length of a clipped interval and counting measure on its endpoint section. For $d\ge2$, on an interval between vertex heights a face of $K$ is crossed exactly when the height is strictly between its smallest and largest vertex heights. Each such face is cut through its relative interior, so its intersection gives a section face of dimension one less. Conversely each section face is obtained by intersecting the active original facets, and the relative interiors determine the unique corresponding original face. Thus the section face poset stays fixed. Its vertices come from a fixed list of crossed edges and depend affinely on the height. Translate the sections to $u^\perp$. A fixed pulling order gives a fixed simplicial triangulation of the section on the height interval, since coning from the first vertex over triangulated facets not containing it is determined recursively by the face poset. Each simplex has a volume given by an absolute determinant of affine vertex differences divided by $(d-1)!$. The determinant has a fixed sign on the interval since the simplices there are nondegenerate. Hence the section area is polynomial of degree at most $d-1$. Fubini integrates it to the cap polynomial of degree at most $d$.

Bounded section areas give continuity of the cap at every knot. At a proper section the areas approach its area from both sides. Compactness gives outer containment of projected nearby sections in arbitrarily small neighborhoods of the old section, and convex interpolation of the old section with an interior point on the needed side gives homothetic copies with factors tending to one. The same argument gives the area limit from the body side at a supporting facet, while the other side has zero area. This proves the stated first derivatives. For lower-dimensional supporting sections the inside limit is zero by the same outer containment. The adjacent polynomials supply finite one-sided second derivatives everywhere.

If $q\ne0$, for all sufficiently small positive $t$ the sign of the offset is the sign of $q$, so expanding the appropriate adjacent polynomial yields the displayed coefficients. If $q=0$, the offset is already second order, and the first derivative from the side of $r$ gives $D(r)$ as the second coefficient, including zero when $r=0$.
statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact polytope and $u$ a unit vector. Then $F(T)=|K\cap\{u\cdot X\ge T\}|$ is continuous and polynomial of degree at most $d$ between consecutive vertex heights in direction $u$, and constant outside their range. Write $f^\pm$ and $h^\pm$ for its one-sided first and second derivatives at a given $T$. For $t\downarrow0$,
$$
F(T+tq+t^2 r/2)=F(T)+tD(q)+t^2 E(q,r)/2+o(t^2),
$$
where $D(0)=0$, $D(q)=f^{\operatorname{sgn}(q)}q$ if $q\ne0$, $E(0,r)=D(r)$, and $E(q,r)=h^{\operatorname{sgn}(q)}q^2+f^{\operatorname{sgn}(q)}r$ if $q\ne0$. At an inside supporting facet of area $S$, $D(q)=-S\max(q,0)$. At an outside supporting facet of area $S$, $D(q)=S\max(-q,0)$. At a proper cut the two first derivatives agree and equal minus the section area.
title: One-sided parallel cap two-jets of a polytope
